items.title: How to Change Your Life
items.description: HOW TO CHANGE YOUR LIFE by Maria Popova Don’t try to wash your tired hands clean from the bloodshed of your private wars. Just unclench the fist that has come to feel like home and let the story slip between your trembling fingers into the river of time, silver and indifferent. You may have to kneel for days        or decades in a pool of silence blue and lonely as a heron but it will be there, the small green stone lying at the bottom lustrous with a peace        larger than joy. items.title: The Fascinating Science of How We Think Not with the Brain But with the World
items.description: "By reaching beyond the brain... we are able to focus more intently, comprehend more deeply, and create more imaginatively — to entertain ideas that would be literally unthinkable by the brain alone."

items.title: I Long to Read More in the Book of You: Moomins Creator Tove Jansson’s Tender and Passionate Letters to the Love of Her Life
items.description: "I’m so unused to being happy that I haven’t really come to terms with what it involves... I feel like a garden that’s finally been watered, so my flowers can bloom."

items.title: The Unspeakable World: Alan Watts on How to Touch the Pulse of Life
items.description: What makes life so disorienting is that its greatest revelations and greatest transformations are inarticulable. William James knew this when he listed ineffability as the first of the four features of transcendent experiences. Everything beautiful and meaningful, from the grand elations to the small gladnesses that make life worth living, is irreducible to words, is sand slipping through the fingers of language as we try to capture it. items.title: How to Be a Good Explorer on the Lifelong Expedition to Yourself
items.description: Life is an ongoing expedition into the brambled tendrilled wilderness of ourselves, continually stymied by all we mistake for a final destination — success, superhuman strength, the love of another. Along the way, we keep confusing experiment and exploration. An experiment proves or disproves an existing theory; its payoff is data, fixed and binary. items.title: Why Leaves Change Color and How We Become Who We Are: The Science of Chlorophyll and the Poetics of Personhood
items.description: "We reach forth and strain every nerve, but we seize only a bit of the curtain that hides the infinite from us."

items.title: How Not to Waste Your Wildness
items.description: "What is wild cannot be bought or sold, borrowed or copied. It is. Unmistakable, unforgettable, unshamable, elemental as earth and ice, water, fire and air, a quintessence, pure spirit, resolving into no constituents. Don't waste your wildness: it is precious and necessary. In wildness, truth."

items.title: The Day Dostoyevsky Discovered the Meaning of Life in a Dream
items.description: "And it is so simple... You will instantly find how to live."

items.title: How to Break Free from the Tyranny of Certainty: The Japanese Concept of “Ma”

items.title: Albert Camus on the Source of Strength and How to Save Our Sanity in Trying Times
items.description: "In the depths of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer."

items.title: Kahlil Gibran on the Courage to Weather the Uncertainties of Love
items.description: "Think not you can direct the course of love, for love, if it finds you worthy, directs your course."

items.title: The Paradoxes and Possibilities of Transformation: Adam Phillips on Our Ambivalent Desire for Change
items.description: "There is no description of a life without an account of the changes that are possible within it."

items.title: Polyvagal Theory and the Neurobiology of Connection: The Science of Rupture, Repair, and Reciprocity
items.description: "The mind narrates what the nervous system knows. Story follows state."

items.title: A Beginning, Not a Decline: Colette on the Splendor of Autumn and the Autumn of Life
items.description: In praise of "the gaiety of those who have nothing more to lose and so excel at giving."

items.title: The New Science of Plant Intelligence and the Mystery of What Makes a Mind
items.description: "Every thought that has ever passed through your brain was made possible by plants."
